To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We developed a novel functional screening approach to identify miRNAs that regulate the post‐transcriptional control of GPC3, a major oncogene in HCC; (2) Using this approach, we identified five miRNas, miR‐96/miR‐1271 and miR‐129/miR‐1303, that control GPC3 levels; (3) We found that miR-1271 is down-regulated in HCC and

using a FunREG‐based screen, we identified five miRNas that regulate GPC3 expression and that the down‐regula tion of one of them, miR‐ 1271, is associated with the up‐regu lation of GPC3 in a subgroup of HCCC and contributes to the oncogenic effect of GPC3 overex pression.

(1) We developed a functional screening approach to identify microRNA‐regulated genes; (2) Using this method, we identified five microRNA that target GPC3; (3) We demonstrated that GPC3 is overexpressed in a subgroup of hepatocellular carcinoma and inversely correlates to the expression of one microRNA, miR‐1‐27‐1.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of miRNAs that control GPC3 in HCC cells, the functional characterization of these miRNAs, and their potential use as biomarkers for the diagnosis of HCC and for the development of therapeutic strategies.
